image_description: A large pelican standing on green grass with tall reeds in the background. The bird has white and grey plumage, a long pinkish-orange bill with a visible gular pouch, and dark flight feathers on its wings. It is facing right, with its neck curved and legs visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bill with distensible gular pouch extending from lower mandible.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows a massive bill with a distinct, sagging gular pouch characteristic of pelicans.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bill is enormous and elongated, vastly exceeding head length, with bright orange, yellow, or pink coloration during breeding.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is significantly longer than the head and exhibits pink/orange hues consistent with breeding plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large with prominent pouch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head structure is proportional to the body, and the pouch is the dominant feature of the lower face.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plumage is predominantly white, grey, or brown depending on species and season.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bird displays white body feathers with grey/brown shading on the wings and back, matching typical pelican coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits heavy barrel-shaped torso of very large proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The torso appears robust and barrel-shaped, supporting the large wing structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings are extremely broad and long with dark flight feathers contrasting lighter body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The folded wings show clear contrast between the white coverts and the black/dark grey flight feathers at the tips.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and webbed with all four toes connected.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible foot shows the characteristic totipalmate structure (all four toes connected by webbing) and short leg proportion.
The neck is visibly long and held in a retracted, curved posture typical of pelicans on land.
The tail feathers are short and extend just beyond the folded wings, appearing wedge-shaped.

artifact_observations.location: Feather edges on the back and wing coverts
artifact_observations.reasoning: Some feather boundaries appear slightly soft or 'painted' rather than having crisp individual strand definition, common in AI generation but not structurally failing.
The far foot is partially obscured and blends slightly into the grass, making the exact toe connection ambiguous, though likely due to occlusion rather than generation error.

Webbing connectivity of the feet (totipalmate check)

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the gular pouch and the neck; AI often fails to render the skin texture correctly here. Also, verify that the 'webbed' feet actually show all four toes connected, as AI frequently defaults to standard anisodactyl (three forward, one back) bird feet incorrectly.
